summary: Ying-shih Yü was a scholar in sinology, history and archaeology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Harvard after studies at Yenching, New Asia College, and CUHK. He held professorships at Michigan, Harvard, Yale, and Princeton, and led New Asia College.

Yinggang Sun is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Sun held a post at Fudan University (attested 2014) and served as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yingshan Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen held posts at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, serving as professor (attested 1996) and later as an honorary research fellow (attested 2026; retired in February 2023).
Yingxue Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Wang completed a BA at Yale University (2013–2017) and an MA at Harvard University (2017–2025).

Yinke Chen worked in sinology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied across Europe and at Harvard under Lanman, Lüders, Müller, and Haenisch. His career included professorships at Tsinghua, Peking University, Academia Sinica, and Sun Yat-sen University.

Yinshun was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and Qingnian, and earned a doctorate from Taisho University. He taught at Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes, led Fawang Buddhist Institute, and served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.
Yirmiyahu Yovel was a scholar of philosophy. He studied at the Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1956–1968), and Princeton University (~1966–1968).
Yiu Wing Chan works in Buddhist studies. Chan earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong in 2013, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann was a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv, Hanazono, and Kyoto University (PhD), and under Sojo Hirano and Ben-Ami Scharfstein, later serving as professor at the University of Haifa (~1975–2005).

Yogendra Bhardwaj works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Bhardwaj earned a PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University (2018–2021) and was appointed assistant professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2025.
Yohei Furukawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Having studied under Takatsugu Hayashi, Furukawa has held a post as associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

Yohei Kawajiri is an Indology and philosophy scholar. Kawajiri worked at Chikushi Jogakuen University as a research associate (attested 2008–2013) and later staff (attested 2022), and was a JSPS special research fellow (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and served as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003, 2015).
Yoichi Kawada is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He served as director of the Institute of Oriental Philosophy (attested 2002 and 2016).
Yong Hua specializes in Buddhist studies. Hua earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014) under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. Trained at Menri, Tingchen, and Yungdrung Ling, he became lopön of Menri and founded Triten Norbutse Monastery. He was also a visiting scholar at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy figure who studied at Sherab Ling Monastery, Dzongsar Institute, and under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche. He has served as abbot of Sherab Ling Monastery.
Yongshan He is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2011) and also studied under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tsinghua and Harvard under Lanman and Babbitt. He was a professor and vice-president at Peking University, and also taught at Southeast, Nankai, and Southwestern Associated universities.

Yongyu Chen has worked in Buddhist studies. Chen earned a BA at Cornell University, was a PhD student at Harvard, served as a professor at Joong-Ang Sangha University (attested 2015), and became an ArtTable Fellow at the Public Art Fund in 2025.
